cases.reviewerAnswer: Use hay to introduce existence and estar to locate an identifiable entity: Hay un banco en la calle. / El banco está en la calle.

cases.reviewerAnswer: Hay un libro en la mesa. Hay unas sillas. No hay leche. ¿Hay un hotel aquí? Impersonal present-tense hay does not change with the number of the following noun.

cases.defect: This states an unrestricted word-order rule that is false. A Spanish question can place a subject or topic before the interrogative word, as in ¿Tú dónde estás?, or begin with a preposition, as in ¿De dónde eres? The provided clip follows one common pattern, not a universal rule.
cases.correction: Limit the hint to this recording: explain that dónde means «де» and identifies a question about location. Remove the claim that every question with an interrogative word begins with that word.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 42, treatment of interrogative constructions, interrogative phrases and preceding topics (from memory).
